title: Community Health Nursing
description: Primary health care, community diagnosis, home visiting, immunisation and the cold chain, school and occupational health, and family planning in Nigeria.

topics.title: Primary Health Care
topics.summary: Alma-Ata and Astana declarations, principles and components of PHC, and PHC in Nigeria.

notes.b: The Alma-Ata Declaration (1978, USSR — now Kazakhstan) defined primary health care (PHC) as essential health care based on practical, scientifically sound and socially acceptable methods, universally accessible to individuals and families through their full participation, at a cost the community and country can afford — the strategy for 'Health for All by the year 2000'. The Astana Declaration (2018) renewed this commitment towards universal health coverage. Principles: equity, community participation, intersectoral collaboration, appropriate technology, and focus on prevention and promotion.
k: Principles: equity, participation, intersectoral collaboration, appropriate technology

notes.b: The eight essential elements of PHC (ELEMENTS mnemonic): Education about health problems, Locally endemic disease control, Expanded programme of immunisation, Maternal and child health including family planning, Essential drugs, Nutrition and food supply, Treatment of common diseases and injuries, Safe water and sanitation (Nigeria added mental health, dental health and others). In Nigeria, PHC is the responsibility of local government areas, coordinated by the National Primary Health Care Development Agency (NPHCDA) under the 'PHC Under One Roof' policy. The Ward Health System makes the political ward the operational unit, with Ward Development Committees. Community health extension workers (CHEWs) and community health officers deliver much care under the Standing Orders.
k: PHC run by LGAs; coordinated by NPHCDA

topics.title: Community Diagnosis and Home Visiting
topics.summary: Steps of community diagnosis, health indicators, family health assessment and home visits.

notes.b: Community diagnosis identifies the health status, problems, needs and resources of a community as a basis for planning. Steps: entry into the community (courtesy visits to traditional rulers, religious and opinion leaders), data collection (demographic, socio-economic, environmental, health service and morbidity/mortality data using surveys, observation, records, key informant interviews and focus groups), analysis, prioritisation of problems (magnitude, severity, feasibility, community concern), planning interventions, implementation and evaluation. Common indicators: crude birth and death rates, infant mortality rate (deaths under 1 year per 1,000 live births), under-five mortality rate, maternal mortality ratio (maternal deaths per 100,000 live births), immunisation coverage and access to safe water.

Home visits allow nurses to assess the family in its environment, provide care and health education, and follow up mothers, newborns, the elderly and patients with chronic diseases (e.g. TB, HIV). Principles: purposeful and planned; respect the family's culture and privacy; involve the family; maintain confidentiality; use the 'bag technique' (nursing bag with infection-control procedures — clean and dirty sides, handwashing); document findings; and follow up. Family health assessment considers structure (nuclear, extended, polygamous), roles, communication, resources and the family life cycle.

topics.title: Immunisation and the Cold Chain
topics.summary: Nigeria's routine immunisation schedule, vaccine storage, and adverse events following immunisation.

notes.b: Nigeria's routine immunisation schedule (National Programme on Immunisation, managed by NPHCDA) includes: at birth — BCG, OPV0 and hepatitis B birth dose; 6, 10 and 14 weeks — pentavalent vaccine (DPT-HepB-Hib), pneumococcal conjugate vaccine (PCV), OPV, rotavirus (6 and 10 weeks) and IPV (at 14 weeks, with fractional doses in some schedules); 9 months — measles (first dose), yellow fever and meningococcal A conjugate (MenA), plus vitamin A; 15 months — second measles dose (MCV2). HPV vaccine was introduced in 2023 for girls aged 9–14 years. Supplementary campaigns (e.g. polio, measles) complement routine immunisation.
k: 6/10/14 weeks: pentavalent, PCV, OPV (+ rotavirus, IPV)

notes.b: The cold chain keeps vaccines at the recommended temperature from manufacture to administration. Most vaccines are stored at +2 °C to +8 °C; oral polio vaccine may be stored frozen at central levels. Freeze-sensitive vaccines (pentavalent, hepatitis B, PCV, IPV, HPV, tetanus-containing) are damaged by freezing — the shake test detects frozen adsorbed vaccines. Vaccine vial monitors (VVM) show cumulative heat exposure: discard when the inner square matches or is darker than the outer circle. Reconstituted BCG, measles and yellow fever vaccines are discarded after 6 hours or at the end of the session. Adverse events following immunisation (AEFI) — e.g. fever, local swelling, BCG ulcer, rare anaphylaxis — must be managed and reported.
k: VVM: discard if inner square ≥ outer circle

topics.title: School, Occupational and Environmental Health Nursing
topics.summary: School health programme, occupational hazards, and water, sanitation and hygiene.

notes.b: The National School Health Policy covers healthful school environment (safe water, toilets, safe buildings), school health services (screening for vision, hearing, dental problems, malnutrition; first aid; immunisation; deworming), skill-based health education (hygiene, nutrition, sexual and reproductive health, drug abuse prevention), school feeding (the National Home-Grown School Feeding Programme) and school–community relationships. Common school-age problems: malaria, helminthiasis, anaemia, visual problems, dental caries, skin infections and injuries.
k: School health: environment, services, education, feeding

notes.b: Occupational hazards: physical (noise, heat, radiation), chemical (dusts, solvents, pesticides — e.g. silicosis in miners, lead poisoning), biological (needlestick injuries, TB in health workers), ergonomic (back injuries in nurses from lifting) and psychosocial (stress, violence). Control follows the hierarchy: elimination, substitution, engineering controls, administrative controls, personal protective equipment. Environmental health covers safe water (boiling, chlorination, filtration, protected wells and boreholes), sanitation (improved latrines, ending open defecation — community-led total sanitation), solid waste management, food hygiene and vector control.
k: Hierarchy of controls: eliminate → substitute → engineer → administrative → PPE
Chlorination and boiling make water safe

topics.title: Family Planning and Reproductive Health
topics.summary: Contraceptive methods, counselling, effectiveness and reproductive health services.

notes.b: Family planning helps individuals and couples achieve desired number and spacing of children, reducing maternal and child deaths. Methods: short-acting hormonal (combined oral contraceptive pill, progestogen-only pill, injectables such as DMPA every 3 months), long-acting reversible contraception (LARC — implants such as Jadelle (5 years) and Implanon (3 years), copper IUD (up to 10–12 years), hormonal IUD), barrier methods (male and female condoms — the only methods that also protect against STIs/HIV), fertility awareness methods (Standard Days, lactational amenorrhoea method — effective for 6 months if exclusively breastfeeding and amenorrhoeic), permanent methods (tubal ligation, vasectomy) and emergency contraception (levonorgestrel within 72 hours, copper IUD within 5 days).
k: LARC: implants, IUDs — most effective reversible methods
LAM: effective 6 months with exclusive breastfeeding
Emergency pill within 72 h; IUD within 5 days

notes.b: Counselling uses the GATHER approach (Greet, Ask, Tell, Help, Explain, Return/Refer) and respects informed, voluntary choice. WHO Medical Eligibility Criteria guide safe method selection: for example, combined oestrogen-containing methods are avoided in women with a history of thrombosis, migraine with aura, breastfeeding under 6 weeks postpartum, and smokers over 35. Effectiveness is compared by failure rates (Pearl Index — pregnancies per 100 woman-years). Post-partum family planning, including IUD insertion within 48 hours of delivery, improves birth spacing (recommended interval at least 24 months before the next pregnancy).
k: Avoid oestrogen in thrombosis history, migraine with aura, smokers > 35
